<Phase type="activation">

Picture a restaurant bill that two people read differently. The waiter sees the total of the order. The owner sees how much of it will go to food, rent and wages.

**There is one number on the bill, but each of them has a different profit behind it.** Keep this bill in mind: what follows is the same story, only with a bigger total.

</Phase>

<Phase type="reflection">

Go back to the bill. The waiter is not lying when they name the total. They simply cannot see the lines the owner sees.

**The venue is not lying either when it says "your profit is the difference between the price and the rate."** It sees its half of the bill. The leader writes the other half themselves.

</Phase>

<Phase type="concept">

## A teaching deal

Let us take round teaching numbers. A week of 6 nights, a full campus for 20 places. The venue's rate is 1,800 dollars per guest. The guest price is 3,000 dollars. All 20 come.

Open the deal in the academy calculator: [teaching deal "a full campus for 20"](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#). The form fills in by itself; you do not need to type anything.

## Two profits

The calculator shows two numbers.

**"Profit" as the venue counts it** is 24,000 dollars. That is (3,000 − 1,800) × 20: the markup over the rate, times guests.

**The leader's honest profit** is 22,200 dollars. The calculator takes the venue and all the leader's costs out of revenue. In the teaching example there is one cost: card payment fees (acquiring) and a refund reserve, 3 % of revenue, which is 1,800 dollars.

The difference between them is the lines the venue does not see: the leader's costs and empty places. The more lines the leader has, the further apart the two profits are.

## Break-even in guests

The third number is **13 guests.** That is the minimum of paying guests at which honest profit does not go negative.

With a full campus, the contract does not shrink with the group. So every guest below twenty takes almost their whole price out of profit, not just the markup.

## What else the page shows

A monthly cash plan and the cash gap: in this example the leader is 17,028 dollars short in the third month. Where the gap comes from and how to close it is the fourth lesson of the module.

The calculator works in your browser. The numbers from the link are not sent anywhere.

<SelfCheck id="c2"/>

</Phase>

<Phase type="practice">

1. Open the [teaching deal](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#) and find three numbers on the page: "profit" as the venue counts it, honest profit and break-even.
2. Change the number of guests from 20 to 18. See how much honest profit fell, and how much the venue's "profit" fell.
3. Open [the same deal, but 12 came](https://academy.synergify.com/en/instrumenty/kalkulyator-retrita/#). Compare: the venue's "profit" is 14,400 dollars, and the leader is 1,080 in the red.
4. Switch the calculator to the venue's view and see what it gets in both cases.
5. Write in one sentence who carries the eight empty places in this model.

</Phase>
